_arch_note: SPARSE-HAMMING (soft_topk) BACKWARD TEST @16K. Fast FastMHL with forward_mode='hybrid_smooth' and the new backward_topk=1: the x/temperature gradient propagates through EXACTLY 2 cells = the main/argmax row + the SINGLE argmin-|d| 1-bit-flip neighbour (alt_index = main ^ flip_mask at p_star=argmin|d|) -- the same 2 rows the hybrid_smooth forward already gathers/blends. The 2-cell backward is a true sparse-row path (_hybrid_smooth_2cell_bwd): elementwise mul+reduce over the 2 gathered rows (no full-K matmul, no topk kernel, no [B,nt,K] tensor), reusing the forward's saved main_index/alt_index/u. Measured on this arch's inner FastMHL shape (B=6144, H4, tph128, nap7->K128, din/dout48): backward 8.73ms(full-K topk=0) -> 4.80ms(topk=1) = 1.82x faster; peak mem 7.28GB -> 1.06GB = 6.84x lower. Forked from exp_n_0187 (Light@48K); ONLY changes vs 0187: lut_impl light->fast, lut_forward_mode hard->hybrid_smooth, ADD lut_backward_topk=1, n_steps 48000->16000, eval_every 500->200 (match 0186's 16K cadence). Everything else identical: CompressionMHL H4/tph128/nap7, d_in48/d_out48, joint false, fp32 tables, seed 1, lut_base_seed 1000, device_batch 12/grad_accum 4 (effective batch 24,576), lr 3e-4, warmup_frac 0.1 (->warmup 1600), lut_forward_confidence true, lut_confidence_form bounded_norm. Trained with train_fixed.py (corrected in-run eval: bs48x100 skip12, held-out shard_06542).
